question: Should `runCommandInherited()` for the postpublish verifier share the 120-second hard SIGKILL deadline used for npm, GitHub, and git probes, or should release verification use command-specific budgets?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes release failure behavior for every inherited subprocess, and the linked daemon precedent covers a different, narrowly bounded lookup rather than this release workflow.

options.title: Use command-specific budgets
options.body: Keep bounded network and metadata commands, but set and document a separately justified postpublish-verifier deadline with focused proof.

options.title: Accept the universal two-minute budget
options.body: Confirm that all release-verifier subprocesses are expected to finish within two minutes and accept timeout failure as the release contract.

recommendation.title: Use command-specific budgets
recommendation.body: Keep bounded network and metadata commands, but set and document a separately justified postpublish-verifier deadline with focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The only concrete nearby history in the supplied context is the merged synchronous-command timeout precedent; confidence is low because release-verifier ownership itself was not established.
